styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Arcaded old streets, temples and the Hainan Museum.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Coconut, seafood and street stalls from morning to late.

styles.label: Beach
styles.blurb: West Coast sands, sunsets and easy swims.

stays.why: Walk to the arcaded old streets, snack stalls and small temples. Central for buses and taxis.
Downtown shopping and food, close to the museum and easy taxi pickups.
Beach resorts and long seaside walks; quieter nights, farther from the old town.
Closest to the airport and the high-speed train station; handy for early flights.

food: Try Hainan staples: Wenchang chicken, coconut rice, and a bowl of Hainan-style noodles for breakfast.
Seafood: pick fish and shellfish at a market or tank restaurant and have it cooked; agree the price per weight first.
Street snacks around Bo'ai Old Street: coconut water, grilled squid and sweet rice cakes, mostly ¥5–20.
Cool down with qingbuliang, a sweet coconut-milk dessert soup with beans and fruit.
Big night food streets and open-air seafood places get busy after 7pm; go early or expect a wait.
more_time: Add a day trip to the volcanic crater park and lava villages north of the city; check opening hours on the day.
Take the high-speed train to Sanya for beaches and resort life, roughly 1.5–2 hours each way.
Slow down on the West Coast: a sunset walk, a beach café and an evening seafood dinner.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the old streets, the museum and a West Coast beach day, with time left for seafood dinners.

month_notes: January: mild and dry-ish, highs near 21°C. Bring a light jacket for evenings.
February: similar to January, around 23°C by day. Good walking weather.
March: warms to 27°C. Comfortable, with about 10 rain days.
April: hot at 30°C and wetter; plan indoor sights for midday.
May: 32°C with frequent rain (about 20 days). Carry a rain jacket.
June: hottest and wettest; highs 33°C. Go out early or after dark.
July: hot and rainy, around 32°C. Expect heavy downpours.
August: the wettest month, about 23 rain days. Keep plans flexible.
September: still hot and wet; typhoon season, so check forecasts.
October: rain eases a little at 28°C. Pleasant evenings return.
November: drier and cooler at 26°C. A good month to visit.
December: mild at 22°C and the driest month. Pack a light layer.

climate_guide.summary: Tropical and humid: warm all year, with a hot, very wet summer and a mild, drier winter.

items.title: Best time: November to March
items.text: Highs of 21–27°C and the fewest rain days. Ideal for walking the old streets and the coast.

items.title: Wet season May to October
items.text: About 19–23 rain days a month, often short heavy showers. Carry a light rain jacket.

items.title: Hot summer
items.text: June peaks near 33°C with warm nights around 27°C. Do outdoor sights early morning.

items.title: Typhoon season
items.text: Late summer and autumn can bring storms. Check forecasts and keep travel plans flexible.

items.title: Humid year-round
items.text: Sea air keeps it muggy, especially May to September. Light, quick-dry clothes help.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light breathable clothes, sunscreen and a hat; a rain jacket in summer; a light layer for winter evenings.

transit.best: Ride-hailing or metered taxis for most trips; buses are cheap but slow.

modes.text: No metro in the city. Don't plan around rail inside Haikou.
Commuter trains on the Hainan high-speed line link the airport and main stations.
City buses are cheap and cover most routes; fares are a few yuan.
Taxis meter from about ¥10; insist on the meter (dabiao). DiDi and Amap work well; Uber does not operate.
Bikes and electric scooters are easy to rent; riverside paths are good.
Ferries cross to Xuwen and Beihai from New Port and Xiuying Port.
Not needed for a city visit; use taxis, buses and trains instead.
Good around Bo'ai Old Street and the waterfront in the cooler months; use rides in summer heat.
